title: Low-voltage wiring and the certificate
why: We size the cables, earth the install, fit the protection, and issue the certificate of compliance against this before handover.

title: Lightning protection of the building
why: A roof with modules gets a lightning protection system bonded to the electrical earth, and the array frame alone is not that system.

title: PV test sheets and handover pack
why: We fill in the inspection sheets and the system record on site and hand them over with the job.

title: Lithium cell safety
why: We look for this safety standard on the battery datasheet before we accept the pack.

title: Grid connection of the inverter
why: We do not commission a grid-tied inverter until the utility has accepted the connection.

title: Inverter safety listing
why: We do not install a PV inverter that has no safety listing to this standard.

title: Medium-voltage cable ends
why: Medium-voltage terminations and joints are made by someone competent for that cable, and we do not leave a screen or an earth tail off.

title: Built switchboard
why: A board we design and populate is checked as a complete assembly, not only as a box of listed parts.

title: Fixed wiring cable
why: Building wire we pull into conduit or trunking is ordered to this, not as a generic flex.

title: Shock protection
why: Bond PV frames and battery and inverter cases to earth and fit the right earth leakage, because a bad earth can leave metal live without tripping.

title: Generator rating
why: We take the generator rating and duty from the machine nameplate before we size the changeover.

title: Supply voltage quality
why: When a site reports dips or flicker we describe them in the utility's terms, and we do not set our own limits.

title: Transformer nameplate
why: We take the rating, vector group and impedance off the transformer nameplate before we set protection or parallel another unit.

title: Socket earth leakage
why: Socket outlets go on earth leakage rated at no more than 30 mA, and we still earth the circuit because that device is extra protection, not a substitute.

title: Lightning risk first
why: We do the lightning risk assessment before we choose the level of protection, and we do not copy the air terminals from the last factory.

title: String polarity and voltage
why: Before we close a DC isolator we check string polarity and open-circuit voltage, and we do not parallel a string that does not match.

title: A cell failure stays put
why: We ask how the pack stops one cell failure from spreading through the bank, and we do not install a battery with no answer.

title: Run only inside the supply band
why: We set the inverter to keep running from 85% to 110% of nominal voltage and from 47 Hz to 51.5 Hz, and to disconnect outside the limits in this specification.

title: Both inverter safety parts
why: We look for both the general power-converter safety part and the particular inverter part. One mark without the other is not the listing we accept.

title: Intake transformer neutral
why: We earth the low-voltage neutral of the intake transformer the way the supply arrangement requires, and we record the earth reading.

title: What the board can carry
why: We use the assembly rated current and its diversity, not the sum of the breaker ratings, when we say what the board can carry.

title: Read the sheath
why: We read the size, voltage and standard on the sheath before the cable is installed. An unmarked drum does not go into a permanent circuit.

title: PV wiring inside the building
why: We install the PV supply so it meets the building wiring rules, not as a separate system with its own habits.

title: Size for the start
why: We size the cable, the breaker and the changeover for the starting current, not only the running current on the nameplate.

title: Record the dip
why: We record a voltage dip by how deep it went and how long it lasted, using the terms in this quality-of-supply specification.

title: Do not parallel unlike transformers
why: We do not parallel two transformers unless the vector groups and the voltage ratios allow it.

title: Volt drop
why: We size every cable so the volt drop from the point of supply to the farthest outlet or fixed appliance stays within 5% at full load.

title: Down conductors
why: Down conductors take a short path to the earth termination, kept clear of the building wiring so a side flash cannot jump across.

title: DC insulation on commissioning
why: Commissioning includes the insulation resistance of the DC circuits, measured with the array isolated.

title: Leave the battery management in
why: We leave the battery management that was tested with the pack in circuit. We do not bypass it to squeeze out more capacity.

title: Wait before reconnecting
why: After a trip the inverter stays off until voltage and frequency have been back inside the normal band for at least 60 seconds.

title: Residual current in the inverter
why: Where the inverter provides the residual-current monitoring this safety standard requires, we do not defeat it with a bypass.

title: Grade the intake protection
why: We grade the intake protection with the utility incomer so a fault on our side does not take out the rest of the feeder.

title: Routine tests on every board
why: Every board we build gets the routine checks of wiring, device operation and dielectric withstand before it leaves the workshop.

title: Fixed cable is not a flex
why: Pendant and trailing flex is ordered to its own standard. We do not hang this fixed-wiring cable as a lead, or pull flex in as permanent wiring.

title: Label the PV isolators
why: The DC and AC isolators for the PV supply are labelled with what they open, so the next person can kill the right one.

title: Continuous duty
why: A machine marked for continuous duty is the one we use as a base load. A short-time rating is not a prime generator.

title: Measure at the point of supply
why: A power-quality complaint is measured at the point of supply. A reading at the far end of our own cable is not the utility's compliance point.

title: Transformer cooling
why: We keep the cooling the nameplate assumes, and we do not box a transformer in so it cannot hold its temperature rise.

title: Distribution board labels
why: We label every circuit on the board and blank every unused opening before we leave the site.

title: Bond the roof metal
why: Gutters, roof sheets and the module frames are bonded into the lightning protection system where that design calls for it.

title: Shutdown order in the pack
why: The handover pack includes the string layout and the order in which to open the DC and AC isolators.

title: Battery system safety
why: We treat the battery, inverter and protection as one storage system, not a loose pack of cells.

title: Stop feeding a dead supply
why: If the supply islands, the inverter stops energising it within 2 seconds, and we prove that by opening the supply breaker.

title: Inverter mounting
why: We mount the inverter inside the temperature and clearances on its listing, not in a sealed ceiling void that will overheat it.

title: Prove the medium-voltage side dead
why: Before anyone works on the medium-voltage side we isolate, lock, test for dead, and apply the earth switch.

title: Board short-circuit rating
why: We do not install a board whose nameplate short-circuit rating is below the fault current at that point.

title: Cable in the sun
why: Cable that stays on the roof is the sunlight-resistant type. Ordinary building wire does not live in the sun.

title: Do not switch the earth
why: We do not switch the protective earth, and we size it so a fault current can flow long enough for the breaker to open.

title: Frame earth and cooling
why: We earth the machine frame and we keep the cooling air path clear. A set boxed in to hide the noise will not hold its rating.

title: Meter to the contract
why: We meter where the supply contract requires, with the accuracy class and the instrument transformers this metering code calls for.

title: Tap position
why: We record the tap position, and we do not move an off-load tap changer while the transformer is energised.

title: Main switch
why: Each distribution board gets a main switch-disconnector where it can be reached, and we mark which position is off.

title: Earth electrodes
why: We design and test the earth electrodes, and we do not take the reading while the soil is wet from rain.

title: Inspect the PV system again
why: A later visit repeats the inspection and the tests. The first commissioning sheet does not stay valid forever.

title: One shutdown for the storage
why: The storage system has one shutdown that opens the battery and stops the converter together, and the people on site know where it is.

title: Direct current into the AC supply
why: We do not accept an inverter that can push direct current into the AC supply above half a percent of its rated current.

title: Leave the rating plate readable
why: The inverter rating plate and the shutdown marking stay readable after we install it. We do not paint over them or build them in.

title: Keep the proven devices
why: Swapping a breaker for another make breaks the assembly verification. We keep the devices the design was proven with.

title: Cable in the ground
why: Cable in the ground is armoured or run in a protective duct. We do not bury ordinary flat wiring in the soil.

title: Overcurrent at the origin
why: Each conductor is protected against overload and short circuit at its origin, unless this part allows the protection to sit at a defined other point.

title: Match the enclosure to the site
why: We match the insulation class and the enclosure on the nameplate to the room or the yard the machine will stand in.

title: Check the metering transformers
why: We check metering current-transformer polarity and burden before we argue with an import or export reading.

title: Earth fault loop
why: We measure the earth fault loop impedance at the main switch and at the end of the circuit, and we do not leave a breaker that cannot clear that fault.

title: Soil resistivity first
why: We measure soil resistivity before we choose rods, tape or a mat, because a rod that worked on the last site may fail here.

title: PV string wiring and DC isolation
why: We set the string layout, the DC cable and the isolation before the modules go down.

title: Access and fire around the storage
why: We plan access, spacing and fire response for the storage system with the building, before the cabinets are hard against a wall.

title: Safety disconnect
why: An inverter-based generator uses a safety disconnect certified to IEC 62109, and a failure in that unit has to disconnect the generator.

title: Inverter stops when the grid drops
why: We leave anti-islanding on and we open the grid breaker to confirm the inverter stops.

title: Breakers and isolators
why: We use each device only for the current, voltage and duty on its label, and we do not put an AC device on a DC string.

title: Aluminium terminations
why: Aluminium conductors get the lugs, compound and torque the maker specifies. A copper lug squeezed onto aluminium is not a joint.

title: Inspection is not enough
why: Verification is inspection plus test, at first commissioning and again on a periodic visit. A walk-through with no tests is not verification.

title: Generator changeover
why: The changeover between grid and generator is a transfer switch rated for that duty, not a pair of ordinary breakers.

title: Do not open a live current transformer
why: We do not open a current-transformer secondary while its primary is live. We short the secondary first.

title: Insulation resistance
why: We measure insulation resistance with the installation isolated, and we do not energise a circuit that fails the test.

title: Electrode joints
why: We choose the electrode metal and the backfill for that soil, and we do not bury a joint that will corrode open.

title: Cold string voltage
why: We calculate the string open-circuit voltage at the coldest temperature that site sees, and we keep it inside the module, cable and inverter limits.

title: Storage that can export
why: Storage that can push power back into the supply is still an embedded generator. We do not enable that path until the utility has accepted it.

title: Embedded generation label
why: We fit a permanent warning on the distribution board that on-site embedded generation is present, before we ask the utility to switch it on.

title: Do not silence island detection
why: We do not switch island detection off to stop nuisance trips. We find the supply problem instead.

title: Marked for isolation
why: A breaker is an isolator only when it is marked for isolation. We do not lock off a device that lacks that marking and call the circuit safe.

title: Hot roof derating
why: A cable through a hot roof space is derated for that temperature. The size that was fine in a cool trench may not carry the load up there.

title: Lock-out and the certificate
why: We lock out and prove the circuit is dead under the Electrical Installation Regulations, and we do not sign a certificate for work we did not inspect.

title: Break before make
why: Unless the utility has accepted parallel running, the transfer switch opens the supply before it closes the generator, so the set cannot feed back.

title: Bidirectional meter
why: A site that can export gets a meter that records both directions. We do not leave a one-way meter in and ignore the export.

title: Polarity
why: We prove polarity so that switches and single-pole protection break the live conductor, not the neutral.

title: Record the earth test
why: The earth resistance result goes on the record with the test method and the weather, not as a bare number.

title: DC isolator rating
why: The array and inverter DC isolators are rated to break direct current at that voltage. An AC switch is not used there.

title: Battery room and cabinet safety
why: We include ventilation, access and isolation of the battery room or cabinet in the install.

title: Neutral bond on backup only
why: A hybrid inverter that backs the building up bonds neutral to earth only on the load side of the open disconnect, never while it is still tied to the utility.

title: Breaking capacity
why: We match the breaker breaking capacity to the fault current at that point. A higher load-current rating does not mean it can break a bigger fault.

title: Certificate when a property is sold
why: A sale needs a valid certificate of compliance under the Electrical Installation Regulations. We do not issue one without the inspection and the tests.

title: Transfer switch fault rating
why: The transfer switch is rated for the fault current at that point as well as the load. We do not fit a changeover that cannot survive a fault.

title: Leave the meter seal
why: We do not cut a utility meter seal. If the meter has to move, the distributor does it or authorises it in writing.

title: Neutral and earth kept apart
why: We do not add a join between neutral and earth on the consumer wiring except at the single point the supply arrangement allows.

title: Confirm the supply earth
why: We confirm whether a new service is TN-C-S or TN-S before we design our earth, because those are the arrangements this standard allows.

title: String overcurrent protection
why: Where parallel strings can back-feed one another, we fit the string overcurrent protection this array design requires.

title: Ventilate a flooded lead-acid room
why: A flooded lead-acid room is ventilated for the hydrogen charging can produce. We do not seal that room to keep the noise in.

title: Generator type test
why: Type testing of the embedded generator against the utility interface belongs here. It is not permission to connect, and the distributor still has to accept the product.

title: Contactor is not an isolator
why: A contactor starts the motor. We still fit a disconnector that can be locked off before anyone works on that machine.

title: A registered person signs
why: Only a registered person, as the Electrical Installation Regulations define one, signs the certificate. An assistant does not sign it.

title: Harmonics and flicker
why: When the supply looks dirty we measure it against this before we treat it as a fault in the plant.

title: Bonding of metalwork
why: We bond incoming metal water pipes and other exposed metal that can become live back to the main earth terminal.

title: Stops at the supply earth
why: This standard ends at the supply earth terminal. The wiring after that point is done to SANS 10142-1.

title: Array frame bonding
why: We bond the module frames and the mounting structure for that duty, and we prove continuity instead of trusting the clamps alone.

title: Battery cable fault current
why: Cables off the battery terminals are sized and protected for the short-circuit current the battery can deliver, close to those terminals.

title: Type-test evidence
why: The application includes the generator type-test evidence this section calls for. A sales brochure is not a substitute.

title: DC rating stands alone
why: For a battery or a PV string we use the direct-current voltage and current on the device label. The AC figures do not carry over.

title: Leave the certificate with the user
why: We hand the certificate to the user of the installation. The regulations require that user to hold a valid one.

title: Check our own distortion first
why: We check whether our inverters and variable-speed drives are the source of the harmonics or the flicker before we send the utility to fix the supply.

title: Bathroom circuits
why: We do not fit an ordinary socket in the bath or shower area, and fittings in that room get the ingress protection the location needs.

title: Not the lightning earth
why: We do not use this distribution-earthing standard to design the lightning earth. That work sits with SANS 10313.

title: Module type approval
why: We check the module datasheet for this qualification before we buy modules.

title: Isolate the battery before work
why: We isolate the battery and prove the terminals dead before we torque or replace a link, and we keep tools off the cells.

title: Small low-voltage grid connection
why: Before we order the inverter we confirm with the municipality or Eskom whether this site uses the simplified connection or the full one.

title: Medium-voltage switchgear
why: The medium-voltage intake uses switchgear built to this, and we do not treat it as a low-voltage board.

title: Report a serious electrical incident
why: Someone killed or badly hurt by electricity, or a dangerous electrical incident, is reported as the Occupational Health and Safety Act requires. The site diary is not the report.

title: Outdoor points
why: An outdoor socket or light is built for the weather, and the socket sits on earth leakage with the other socket outlets.

title: Distributor neutral earth
why: The distributor earths the source neutral so a fault has a path home and the neutral stays near earth. We do not add our own bond beside that one.

title: Nameplate is the test-bench power
why: We use the nameplate current and voltage from this qualification for the string sums, and we do not expect that power on a hot roof.

title: Export limit on a shared supply
why: On a shared low-voltage supply the simplified rules cap one customer's export at a quarter of the utility installed capacity. Above that, the distributor has to study it.

title: Internal arc rating
why: Where the specification asks for an internal-arc classification, we buy gear that has it and we keep the arc vent clear.

title: Lock out the machine
why: Under the Electrical Machinery Regulations we isolate and lock out a generator, motor or transformer before work on it, and we prove it dead.

title: Water heater circuit
why: The geyser is on a circuit sized for that heater, with a local isolator, and it is not tapped off a socket circuit.

title: Lightning design
why: We design the air terminals, down conductors and earth of the lightning system to this, together with SANS 10313.

title: Module mechanical load
why: Modules on a high-wind roof carry this qualification for mechanical load, and we still check the mounting for the wind at that site.

title: Export share of the transformer
why: Under the simplified rules the export on one transformer stays under three quarters of its rating, and the export on the medium-voltage feeder stays under 15% of that feeder's peak, unless the distributor has set a tighter limit.

title: Earthing switch and interlocks
why: We use the earthing switch and the interlocks supplied with the panel, and we do not defeat an interlock to save a step.

title: Enclose the transformer yard
why: A transformer or generator yard is fenced or enclosed, with the danger notice on it, so it is not a shortcut across the site.

title: Alternative supply
why: A generator or backup inverter that is not allowed to run in parallel is changed over so it cannot feed the utility, and the board is labelled.

title: Separation distance
why: We keep the separation between the lightning conductors and the building wiring, or we bond at the points the design requires.

title: Module safety approval
why: We ask for the module safety certificate as well as the type approval before we place the order.

title: Simplified path still needs a type test
why: A plant that fits the simplified size rules is still type-tested to NRS 097-2-1. That path skips the study, not the product tests.

title: Calculate the fault current
why: We calculate the prospective short-circuit current, including the utility contribution and the motors, before we choose the breaker and the cable withstand.

title: Portable electrical tools
why: Portable electrical tools stay maintained and run from a supply with the required earth leakage. A damaged lead comes off the job.

title: Cable after derating
why: We rate the cable for the breaker after grouping, ambient temperature and the way it is installed, not from the size printed on the drum alone.

title: Surge protection with the lightning system
why: Where the lightning design calls for surge protection on the power conductors, we fit coordinated devices so the wiring is not the weak path.

title: Module fire and shock rating
why: We match the module shock and fire behaviour from this safety qualification to the roof we are fixing it to.

title: Apply to the right distributor
why: We apply to the municipality or to Eskom, whichever holds the supply point, and we do not start parallel running on a verbal go-ahead.

title: More than the transformer load current
why: The fault current at the board is not the transformer full-load current. We include the source and the transformer impedance.

title: Fault level at the board
why: The breaker can break the prospective fault current at that board, or we fit upstream protection that backs it up.

title: That distributor's inverter list
why: We install an inverter on that distributor's accepted list. A unit accepted in another town is not automatically accepted here.

title: Protection relay settings
why: We set the overcurrent and earth-fault relays from a grading study, and we do not copy the numbers from the last site.

title: Tests with the certificate
why: The certificate goes out with the inspection and the test readings. We do not sign it from the office.

title: Export can be refused
why: Compliant equipment can still be refused export. If the distributor says zero export, we set that limit and we prove it holds.

title: Match the current transformer
why: The current transformer ratio, class and polarity have to match the relay setting, and we check the polarity before we trust the trip.

title: Unsafe existing wiring
why: On an alteration we do not connect new work onto an existing installation that is unsafe, and the certificate covers the work we inspected.

title: Papers before exporting
why: The application goes in with the single-line diagram, the certificate of compliance and the commissioning sheet, and we do not export before the import-export meter is fitted.

title: Test the relay before load
why: We injection-test the relay before the plant goes on load, and we file the test sheet with the settings.

title: Medium-voltage site intake
why: On a site with a medium-voltage intake we do not use the low-voltage board rules on that side.

title: Above the small-scale band
why: Once the plant is larger than small-scale embedded generation on the low-voltage supply, we stop using these simplified rules and follow the renewable plant grid code.

title: Medium-voltage room
why: The medium-voltage room stays locked and labelled, and only people competent to switch and earth that gear go in.
